questions.subtopic: Integration and definite integrals
questions.explaination: Using integration by parts, $\int_1^x t \ln t \, dt = \left[\frac{t^2}{2} \ln t - \frac{t^2}{4}\right]_1^x = \frac{x^2}{2} \ln x - \frac{x^2}{4} + \frac{1}{4}$. Equating this to $\frac{1}{4}$ gives $\frac{x^2}{4}(2\ln x - 1) = 0$. Since $x > 1$, we have $2\ln x = 1 \implies x = e^{1/2} = \sqrt{e}$.

questions.question_text:
Consider a binary tree 𝑇 in which every node has either zero or two children.
Let 𝑛> 0 be the number of nodes in 𝑇.
Which ONE of the following is the number of nodes in 𝑇 that have exactly two
children?
questions.subtopic: Trees and strictly binary trees
questions.explaination: In any proper (strictly) binary tree with $L$ leaves and $I$ internal nodes (nodes with 2 children), $L = I + 1$. Since $n = L + I = 2I + 1$, the number of internal nodes is $I = \frac{n-1}{2}$.
questions.question_text_latex: Consider a binary tree $T$ in which every node has either zero or two children. Let $n > 0$ be the number of nodes in $T$. Which ONE of the following is the number of nodes in $T$ that have exactly two children?

questions.question_text:
Let 𝐿, 𝑀, and 𝑁 be non-singular matrices of order 3 satisfying the equations
𝐿2 = 𝐿−1 , 𝑀= 𝐿8 and 𝑁= 𝐿2.
Which ONE of the following is the value of the determinant of (𝑀−𝑁)?
questions.subtopic: Matrices and determinants
questions.explaination: From $L^2 = L^{-1}$, multiplying by $L$ gives $L^3 = I$. Then $M = L^8 = (L^3)^2 L^2 = L^2$, and $N = L^2$. Hence $M - N = L^2 - L^2 = O$, whose determinant is $\det(O) = 0$.

questions.question_text:
A machine receives an IPv4 datagram. The protocol field of the IPv4 header has the
protocol number of a protocol X.

Which ONE of the following is NOT a possible candidate for X?

options.D:
Routing Information Protocol (RIP)

Organising Institute: IIT Roorkee

questions.subtopic: Concept of layering: OSI and TCP/IP protocol stacks
questions.explaination: The IPv4 Protocol field identifies the payload carried directly in the IP datagram: ICMP (protocol 1), IGMP (protocol 2), and OSPF (protocol 89). In contrast, RIP runs as an application-layer process encapsulated inside UDP (port 520).
questions.question_text_latex: A machine receives an IPv4 datagram. The protocol field of the IPv4 header has the protocol number of a protocol X. Which ONE of the following is NOT a possible candidate for X?

options.D:
Hello World!d!

Organising Institute: IIT Roorkee

questions.subtopic: Programming in C: pointers and strings
questions.explaination: `stringcopy(a, a + 2)` copies string `"Hello World!"` into the start of array `a`, overwriting the first 12 characters. The copy stops when `*t` hits null terminator without copying the null terminator over `d!`, leaving trailing `d!\0`, resulting in `"Hello World!d!"`.

questions.question_text:
Consider a network that uses Ethernet and IPv4. Assume that IPv4 headers do not
use any options field. Each Ethernet frame can carry a maximum of 1500 bytes in
its data field. A UDP segment is transmitted. The payload (data) in the UDP
segment is 7488 bytes.
Which ONE of the following choices has the CORRECT total number of fragments
transmitted and the size of the last fragment including IPv4 header?
questions.subtopic: Fragmentation and IP addressing
questions.explaination: UDP payload is 7488 bytes + 8 bytes UDP header = 7496 bytes IP payload. Max IP payload per Ethernet fragment is $\lfloor(1500 - 20)/8\rfloor \times 8 = 1480$ bytes. Fragment sizes are 5 fragments of 1480 bytes ($5 \times 1480 = 7400$), leaving $7496 - 7400 = 96$ bytes for the 6th fragment, so total size is $96 + 20 = 116$ bytes.

Let 𝐺1, 𝐺2 be Context Free Grammars (CFGs) and 𝑅 be a regular expression. For a
grammar 𝐺, let 𝐿(𝐺) denote the language generated by 𝐺.
Which ONE among the following questions is decidable?
questions.subtopic: Turing machines and undecidability
questions.explaination: For Context-Free Grammars, emptiness ($L(G) = \emptyset$) is decidable via finding generating non-terminals, whereas equivalence ($L(G_1) = L(G_2)$) and disjointness ($L(G_1) \cap L(G_2) = \emptyset$) are undecidable.

questions.question_text:
Processes 𝑃1, 𝑃2, 𝑃3, 𝑃4 arrive in that order at times 0, 1, 2, and 8 milliseconds
respectively, and have execution times of 10, 13, 6, and 9 milliseconds respectively.
Shortest Remaining Time First (SRTF) algorithm is used as the CPU scheduling
policy. Ignore context switching times.
Which ONE of the following correctly gives the average turnaround time of the four
processes in milliseconds?
questions.subtopic: CPU and I/O scheduling: SRTF
questions.explaination: Using preemptive SRTF: $P_1$ runs [0,2], $P_3$ runs [2,8] (finishes at 8, TAT = $8-2=6$). Then $P_4$ (remaining 9) runs [8,17] (finishes at 17, TAT = $17-8=9$). $P_1$ (remaining 8) runs [17,25] (finishes at 25, TAT = $25-0=25$). $P_2$ runs [25,38] (finishes at 38, TAT = $38-1=37$). Average TAT = $\frac{25 + 37 + 6 + 9}{4} = \frac{76}{4} = 19$ ms.

Shortest Remaining Time First (SRTF) algorithm is used as the CPU scheduling policy. Ignore context switching times. Which ONE of the following correctly gives the average turnaround time of the four processes in milliseconds?

questions.question_text:
An audit of a banking transactions system has found that on an earlier occasion, two
joint holders of account 𝐴 attempted simultaneous transfers of Rs. 10000 each from
account 𝐴 to account 𝐵. Both transactions read the same value, Rs. 11000, as the
initial balance in 𝐴 and were allowed to go through. 𝐵 was credited Rs. 10000 twice.
𝐴 was debited only once and ended up with a balance of Rs. 1000.
Which of the following properties is/are certain to have been violated by the
system?
questions.subtopic: Transactions and concurrency control: ACID properties
questions.explaination: Both transactions read the same uncommitted state and overwrote each other (lost update anomaly), violating Isolation. The final balance violates the database invariant (starting 11000 debited $2 \times 10000$ cannot yield 1000), violating Consistency.
questions.question_text_latex: An audit of a banking transactions system has found that on an earlier occasion, two joint holders of account $A$ attempted simultaneous transfers of Rs. 10000 each from account $A$ to account $B$. Both transactions read the same value, Rs. 11000, as the initial balance in $A$ and were allowed to go through. $B$ was credited Rs. 10000 twice. $A$ was debited only once and ended up with a balance of Rs. 1000. Which of the following properties is/are certain to have been violated by the system?

questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements regarding Breadth First Search (BFS) and
Depth First Search (DFS) on an undirected simple graph G is/are TRUE?

options.A: A DFS tree of 𝐺 is a Shortest Path tree of 𝐺.
options.B: Every non-tree edge of G with respect to a DFS tree is a forward/back edge.
options.C:
If (𝑢, 𝑣) is a non-tree edge of G with respect to a BFS tree, then the distances from
the source vertex 𝑠 to 𝑢 and 𝑣 in the BFS tree are within ±1 of each other.
options.D:
Both BFS and DFS can be used to find the connected components of G.

Organising Institute: IIT Roorkee

questions.subtopic: Graph traversals: BFS and DFS
questions.explaination: In an undirected graph, non-tree DFS edges can only be back edges (B is true). In a BFS tree, cross edges can only exist between the same or adjacent levels, so distances differ by at most $\pm 1$ (C is true). Both can compute connected components (D is true).
questions.question_text_latex: Which of the following statements regarding Breadth First Search (BFS) and Depth First Search (DFS) on an undirected simple graph $G$ is/are TRUE?

options_latex.A: A DFS tree of $G$ is a Shortest Path tree of $G$.
options_latex.B: Every non-tree edge of $G$ with respect to a DFS tree is a forward/back edge.
options_latex.C: If $(u, v)$ is a non-tree edge of $G$ with respect to a BFS tree, then the distances from the source vertex $s$ to $u$ and $v$ in the BFS tree are within $\pm 1$ of each other.
options_latex.D: Both BFS and DFS can be used to find the connected components of $G$.

The following two signed 2’s complement numbers (multiplicand M and
multiplier Q) are being multiplied using Booth’s algorithm:
M: 1100 1101 1110 1101 and Q: 1010 0100 1010 1010
The total number of addition and subtraction operations to be performed is
___________. (Answer in integer)

Organising Institute: IIT Roorkee
questions.subtopic: Number representations and computer arithmetic: Booth's algorithm
questions.explaination: In Booth's algorithm, additions and subtractions occur whenever there is a transition between adjacent bits $(q_i, q_{i-1})$ of multiplier $Q$ with $q_{-1}=0$. Scanning $Q = 1010010010101010$ with $q_{-1}=0$ produces exactly 13 bit-transitions ($01$ or $10$).

questions.question_text:
In a 4-bit ripple counter, if the period of the waveform at the last flip-flop is 64
microseconds, then the frequency of the ripple counter in kHz is ________. (Answer
in integer)
questions.subtopic: Combinational and sequential circuits: ripple counters
questions.explaination: A 4-bit ripple counter divides the clock frequency by $2^4 = 16$. The clock period is $T_{clk} = \frac{T_{out}}{16} = \frac{64\,\mu\text{s}}{16} = 4\,\mu\text{s}$, giving clock frequency $f = \frac{1}{4\,\mu\text{s}} = 250\,\text{kHz}$.
